dossier.architecture: Virtual four-bar arm with telescopic reach and wide direct gripper.

subsystems.drivetrain: Custom Colson wheels on swerve were chosen for traction, including on the station surface.
subsystems.intake: Curved dual-piece roller gripper; broad acquisition aperture reduces station alignment demand.
subsystems.transfer: Direct grip; no separate handoff described.
subsystems.scoring: Virtual four-bar geometry covers floor, station and scoring poses; extension supplies additional reach.
subsystems.controls: Helix Navigator paths, joint feedback and gravity compensation.

versions: Week-one prototype acquired pieces but did not place them well; curved final geometry addressed placement as well as acquisition.
dossier.analysis: An intake should be evaluated through release and placement, not solely whether it can grab an object. Traction choices must also be judged on the actual obstacle surface.
limits: Interview configuration and reported revisions are documented; full season chronology remains to be audited against the linked releases.

context_documents.title: 2023-3538 · A virtual linkage must preserve useful contact at every task pose
context_documents.body:
# 2023-3538: A virtual linkage must preserve useful contact at every task pose

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A curved roller gripper directly acquires both pieces on a virtual-four-bar/extension architecture. Linkage/sprocket geometry serves floor, station and scoring positions; holding rollers idle at lower speed in the last useful direction.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team identifies fast cycles and a wide acquisition aperture as priorities, and describes testing drivetrain/contact choices for charge-station traction.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A virtual linkage can coordinate joints mechanically, but its coupled path still needs field/robot clearance. Idle roller direction must match possession state or it can eject the wrong piece.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test every acquisition/release pose, interrupted transitions and low-speed holding under chassis acceleration.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/wmEajgIojAA](https://youtu.be/wmEajgIojAA)

source_reviews.title: 3538 RoboJackets | Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the publisher's introduction and AlexZ's fabrication reply.
source_reviews.facts: The introduction identifies Colson swerve, auto intake, arm placement and Helix Navigator. AlexZ says the hubs and Colson wheels were machined in-house and fit MK4 and MK4i.
source_reviews.limitations: Compatibility does not establish which module was installed. The introduction is a secondary summary.

source_reviews.title: 3538 RoboJackets interview
source_reviews.review_basis: Inherited interview synopsis. Full captions not available for this review.
source_reviews.facts: The dossier describes a curved roller tool, virtual four-bar with extension, gravity compensation and pitch-based balancing.
source_reviews.limitations: Inherited details are provisional. No independent visual or full-caption review.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: The RoboJackets' retained interview account describes a single tool that picks up cones and cubes and carries them all the way to the node. The important mechanical distinction is that the tool's angle is tied to the arm geometry, while extension adds reach. This couples the design of the gripper mouth to the poses the arm can reach. The separate fabrication reply directly establishes how the team made its Colson wheel hardware compatible with commercial swerve modules.
piece_flow: Present the curved tool at the floor or station. The older account describes a wide opening intended to tolerate station alignment error.
Draw the piece into the tool and hold it during arm motion. The focused supplement describes reducing roller speed in the previous useful direction.
Move the loaded linkage and extension to the scoring pose, release and recover to a travel pose. The older account describes direct grip without an intermediate transfer.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Treat the mechanism's swept volume as the union of the arm, extension, tool, harness and the retained cone or cube. Mechanically coupled tool angle can simplify commands, but it removes a free adjustment for clearing the bumper or approaching a node at a different angle. A configuration that works at both endpoints can still intersect the grid during the transition.

subsystems.name: Virtual four-bar and extension
subsystems.construction: Older dossier describes a virtual four-bar and telescoping reach.
subsystems.operation: The linked motion carries the same tool from pickup to scoring poses.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older synopsis reports fast cycles as a design priority. The exact choice of linkage is unexplained.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Compare load-dependent tip sag and endpoint error at high reach with error at floor height. Extension can multiply angular play into translational error.
subsystems.interfaces: Linkage geometry sets the tool approach angle, while extension changes reach and the loaded moment on the arm.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect joint play, phase/indexing and carriage travel after impacts. These are proposed checks.
subsystems.unknowns: Link ratios, actuators, travel and event configurations.

subsystems.name: Curved direct gripper
subsystems.construction: Older dossier describes a curved dual-piece roller tool.
subsystems.operation: Acquire, hold at reduced output and release with the same mechanism.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older account reports that the wide opening reduced station alignment demand and that the first prototype acquired better than it placed.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A broad entrance helps only if it leads to a repeatable seat. Compare cone yaw and cube offset at pickup against actual release error.
subsystems.interfaces: Needs tool clearance and roller contact across floor, shelf and node poses.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test restarts after reversing direction and retention during chassis braking. A direction remembered from the previous action could become wrong after an interrupted cycle.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact profile, compression and state logic.

subsystems.name: Colson swerve and station control
subsystems.construction: Machined hubs and wheels were reported by AlexZ. Older account associates gyro pitch with balance.
subsystems.operation: Swerve aligns the collector and traverses the station. The reported balancing loop uses pitch.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older dossier attributes traction selection in part to the station surface.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Test wheel retention and braking on the relevant surface. Wheel compatibility alone does not establish grip, wear or stop distance.
subsystems.interfaces: Changing wheels may alter approach behavior and odometry scale.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check hub attachment and tread wear before attributing variation to software.
subsystems.unknowns: Installed module, wheel dimensions and measured traction.

revisions: Older synopsis separates the week-one pickup prototype from the later curved placement geometry. July reply dates wheel documentation, not installation.
transferable_principles: Prototype pickup, carried pose and release on a single fixture before freezing the virtual-linkage geometry.
disconfirming_conditions: Reject the transfer if tight release-angle tolerances require a separate wrist adjustment or if loaded extension shifts the gripper outside the placement tolerance.
remaining_gaps: Full interview captions, arm CAD and measured repeatability.
recommended_images: Retrieve a source-linked side view with the linkage and extension visible and a close-up of the Colson hub. No image was reviewed.
